picks.title: Kling AI Opens Kling 4.0 to All Users
picks.excerpt: Kuaishou's Kling AI opened Kling 4.0 to all users on klingai.com, adding up to 30-second native clips, multi-reference controls, stereo audio with multilingual lip sync, and MCP and CLI workflow hooks; 4K and 10-bit HDR output are due soon.
picks.rationale: Kling 4.0 is now open to everyone, with 30-second native clips, multi-reference control, lip-synced audio and MCP/CLI hooks. Motion designers can use it in their pipelines today.

picks.title: Meshy Edit, for part-level changes to AI-generated 3D models, launched
picks.excerpt: Meshy Edit, built on a new in-house model, lets users lasso a region of a 3D model, describe a change in text (with up to five reference images) and send the result straight to a slicer, keeping the original intact.
picks.rationale: Meshy Edit is a new release that lets you lasso part of a generated 3D model, change it with a text prompt and send it straight to a slicer. That fixes a common problem: having to regenerate the whole model to change one part.

picks.title: How to build a brand foundation with AI without losing your craft
picks.excerpt: A practical walkthrough of using Claude plus a handful of guardrails to build a brand foundation and design system that developers respect and clients can actually ship.
picks.rationale: A step-by-step guide to using Claude, with guardrails, to build a brand foundation and design system that can actually ship. Brand designers can reuse the process directly.

picks.title: Enforcing Accessibility Gates in Component Libraries: plugin87/ux-ui-agent-skills Review
picks.excerpt: Battle-testing an LLM agent skill set that blocks merges for real WCAG violations in a component library, instead of generating compliant-looking code that breaks screen readers.
picks.rationale: A hands-on test of an agent skill set that blocks merges when a component library has real WCAG violations. Design-system teams get a concrete accessibility gate for AI-written code.

picks.title: Design in the material you ship
picks.excerpt: Designers should understand code the way an architect understands stone: what it can do, not how to cut it. AI now does the cutting, so the same card can be designed in the browser with real data rather than in a static file.
picks.rationale: Argues that AI now does the coding, so designers should design in the browser with real data instead of static files. It shows a concrete shift in where design work happens.
